CITI'S TAKE 
Intel reports earnings on July 23 after the market close. Our 2Q26 sales/EPS 
of $14.4B (up 6% Q/Q)/$0.24 is above Consensus of $14.36B/$0.21 and we 
model 3Q26 sales/EPS of $15.1B (up 5% Q/Q)/$0.29, above Consensus on 
CPU upside and opex discipline. We expect data center sales to upside in 
2026 driven by better-than-expected CPU demand and custom ASIC sales. 
We model Intel foundry sales to scale in 2027 driven by EMIB packaging,
source_file: data/inputs/reports/INTEL/2026-07-15-Citi-Intel Corp (INTC.O)_ Preview_ Investor Focus on Foundry Customers & CPU Demand.pdf

text:
Apple, Nvidia, Media Tek, and Terafab. Maintain Buy. 
Expect 2026 data center upside — We model Intel’s data center segment to grow 
to $23.1B in 2026 (up 37% YoY), above Consensus of $22.8B (up 35% YoY) on better-
than-expected server CPU demand and ASIC business scaling. Intel’s ASIC IPU 
business (e.g. Google Mount Evans) is now running north of $1B in annualized 
revenue and we expect LLM maker using TPUs to layer on the top of it.
Intel foundry sales to scale in 2027 — We model Intel external foundry sales of 
$4.6B in 2027 and $10B in 2028 driven by EMIB packaging and multiple foundry 
wafer customers. Moreover, Intel should be a major beneficiary of Space X initiative
source_file: data/inputs/reports/INTEL/2026-07-15-Citi-Intel Corp (INTC.O)_ Preview_ Investor Focus on Foundry Customers & CPU Demand.pdf

text:
to support Terafab, in our view (please see Citi’s SPCX initiation). 
Expanding Ireland Fab Capacity — This week, Intel announced a $5.7B capex 
investment to expand and upgrade Ireland fab. The news supports CPU demand and 
is a positive readthrough for Intel Foundry. CEO Lip Bu has previously stated “I think 
the best indication, when you see I increase my capex, I’m putting money to buy 
equipment, that means I have real customers. That’s the discipline I have.”
Expect below Seasonal 2H26 on CCG — Intel expects client CPU sales to increase 
in 2Q26 (Citi up 2% Q/Q) and previously expects a below seasonal 2H26 with PC
source_file: data/inputs/reports/INTEL/2026-07-15-Citi-Intel Corp (INTC.O)_ Preview_ Investor Focus on Foundry Customers & CPU Demand.pdf

text:
CPU TAM to be down low double digits Y/Y in 2026 on memory supply constraints.
Focus on the call — We believe the key focus areas on the call are: 1) Intel Foundry 
customer traction, 2) Server CPU demand and TAM assumptions, 3) Capex outlook, 
4) 18A and 14A progress, and 5) PC outlook.

Company description
Intel is a semiconductor company that specializes in microprocessors and is 
the #1 supplier of microprocessors for desktop PCs, notebook PCs, and 
servers with approximately 60% total market share. Intel also has a foundry 
business. Based in Santa Clara, CA, Intel has roughly 83,200 employees 
worldwide. Intel derives approximately 90% of its total revenue and 90% of
source_file: data/inputs/reports/INTEL/2026-07-15-Citi-Intel Corp (INTC.O)_ Preview_ Investor Focus on Foundry Customers & CPU Demand.pdf

text:
total profits from the PC and Datacenter segments. Intel is a vertically 
integrated device manufacturer (IDM) with front-end wafer fabrication 
facilities in Oregon, Arizona, New Mexico, China, Ireland, and Israel and back-
end assembly and test operations in Malaysia, China, Costa Rica, and 
Vietnam.
Investment strategy
We are Buy rated on Intel shares given the AI-driven CPU cycle and we're more 
positive on Intel foundry given better execution by Intel management.
Valuation
We value INTC based on our SOTP valuation, our price target is $130. We 
apply a SOTP valuation framework to each of Intel’s reportable segments and 
to highlight our growth expectations for Intel Foundry.

Risks
PC end-market: Intel derives roughly 90% of sales from the PC and server 
segments, which are highly dependent on IT spending. Therefore, any major 
uptick/downtick in IT spending could result in upside/downside to our 
estimates and cause us to reassess our rating on INTC.
M&A: If Intel engages in a substantial accretive acquisition, it could result in 
upside to our estimates.
Competition: Intel competes directly with AMD in the microprocessor market. 
Consequently, any fluctuations in market share between Intel and AMD could 
result in risk to our estimates.
source_file: data/inputs/reports/INTEL/2026-07-15-Citi-Intel Corp (INTC.O)_ Preview_ Investor Focus on Foundry Customers & CPU Demand.pdf

Customer risk: Intel’s largest PC OEM customers collectively represent 
roughly 45% Intel’s revenue. As a result, any major declines in orders from PC 
OEMs could have a negative effect on our estimates for Intel.
Macroeconomic: Intel’s geographic exposure spans multiple geographies 
including the U.S., Europe, and Asia. As a result, any prolonged 
macroeconomic downturn/upturn could result in downside/upside to our 
estimates and rating.
